Pick representative samples with apricot MaxCoverage

Source: R/subset_samples.R
subset_samples_xcms.Rd

A sample "covers" a feature when its intensity is at or above that feature's q_prob quantile across samples (missing values count as 0). apricot's MaxCoverageSelection then picks the subset_size samples that together cover the most features. Needs Python with apricot-select and numpy (via reticulate).

Usage

subset_samples_xcms(
  msobject,
  msassay,
  subset_size = 100L,
  q_prob = 0.9,
  subsample = TRUE
)

Arguments

msobject

An XcmsExperiment/XCMSnExp.

msassay

Samples × features intensity matrix; rownames(msassay) must be basename(xcms::fileNames(msobject)).

subset_size

Number of samples to keep.

q_prob

Per-feature quantile that defines "covered".

subsample

If FALSE, return every sample and skip Python.

Value

List with msobject (subsetted), assay (selected rows), peaks and all_files (both from the unsubsetted object, so peakidx and sample indices stay valid).
